To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gender segregation in employment structure of the Russian regions has a significant level and the share of men and women in the same economic activities has a tendency to decrease over the period under study.
the level of gender segregation in the structure of employed in the Russian regions is high, and it is not reduced in recent years.

1) the level of gender segregation in the regional employment is characterized by the index of dissimilarities, which reflects the degree of the deviation of the actual distribution of men and woman in the regional employment from the equal distribution; 2) in the regional employment, the gender segregation is characterized by the presence of the spheres of activity with a high concentration of men and woman, which is reflected in the values of the index of the dissimilarities of the distribution of employees by economic activities;
In summary, our research is concerned with
the gendered nature of the regional employment structure.
the gender differences in employment in the regional economy of the Russian Federation.
the following questions: What is the level of gender segregation in the regional employment?

the use of the index dissimilarity allowed to identify the share of employers in the same gender, that should have changed the economic activity in case if employers of another gender would remain at their workplaces, in order to reach the equality of distribution of men and woman by the economic activities.
the gender wage gap is not the result of discrimination alone, but rather a result of a combination of several factors.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the methodology of the analysis of the dynamics of gender segregation at the labour market is developed.

gender inequality in the labour market is a global phenomenon that is not limited to a specific country, but it is also present in the Russian labour market, which is characterized by the high level of gender segregation of the employed by economic activities.

the gender segregation is a serious problem for the regional labour market, which is not only caused by the differences in the preferences of employers and employees but also reflects the real employment opportunities for women and men in different economic activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is necessary to implement the measures of gender equality at the regional labour market, because the reduction of gender segregation will lead to the increase of the efficiency of labour resources and, consequently, will improve the economic development.

the use of a methodology based on the analysis of changes in the structure of employment by gender allows identifying the processes, which facilitate the increase or reduction of the gender asymmetry in a regional employment structure.
gender segregation at the labour market can be studied by the use of a variety of methods.
